doc.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015

chapter: Session stories and why he was hired
title: Why Bucky got the calls: rhythm guitar and the Doublemint commercial
summary: Bucky says he was hired as a rhythm guitarist, unlike soloists such as Caiola and Mottola, follows Freddie Green and Barry Galbraith, and earns residuals from Doublemint and soap operas.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Has a discography been kept on you? I mean I know you can see like all the albums under your names, you know, all the Arbors Records and all that. But is there any kind of record?
No. I don’t know. Maybe. I couldn’t tell.

Sounds like some kind of project for somebody to do. Okay so this is sort of an obvious question. But why did you and Barry Galbraith and Milt Hinton, how come you were on the A team? Why was it that you got the calls?

I don’t know, because I thought maybe because I played rhythm guitar, and there was always room on a recording session to play rhythm. And that’s what I was known for. Al Caiola and Tony Mottola were known for soloists. George Barnes as a soloist. If they didn’t need a soloist they wouldn’t hire them. They just had rhythm guitar. That’s one thing they had to have on a record. Bomp-chink, bomp-chink. And that I knew I could do very well.
Did Freddie Green hip you to that?

Well I followed what Freddie did. But I also knew what Barry Galbraith did. I mean he was with Claude Thornhill’s band and it was superb playing. And I got to know him very well. We played together. We were on the Wrigley Spearmint Gum commercial. Double Your Pleasure or something like that.
Double your pleasure, double your fun, with —
We made a lot of money on that date.
Well they played it — Super Bowl Sunday came around and we ended up with five thousand dollars in the mailbox.
I was going to ask you — do checks still show up for things you did years ago?
No, not like that, not with that price tag on it.
Okay but do you get some mysterious checks sometimes?

Yeah, yeah, yeah. Well I mean I did a lot of soap operas, what was the Irish one there, “Ryan’s Hope.” And they released all the stuff that I was on and they played them all again. I made a lot of money.
Nice. It’s nice when the system works like that right?
